title: fix(kernel): preserve validated STEP edges when healing exceeds the gap limit
body:
### Change

If healing removes edges and the healed solid fails the 0.001 mm endpoint limit, the STEP importer checks the original solid. It keeps the original edges only if the source meets that limit and passes the existing integrity and measurement checks and Solidcore's full level 2 validation. The mesher still checks the requested chord tolerance.

The importer checks endpoint gaps before computing volume and area. It polls for cancellation before rebuilding the source, before level 2 validation and before integration. It integrates only the selected body. When the source exceeds the endpoint limit, the refusal gives the source gap, limit, input-record edge index, vertex coordinates, edge counts and healed gap.

### Results on the reported part

The patched kernel importer still refuses the Fusion heater block. The source endpoint gap is 0.007736 mm, above the 0.001 mm limit. The worst source endpoint is on input-record edge 647 (zero-based). Healing reduces the edge count from 999 to 998 and increases the maximum gap to 0.011573 mm. The reader does not expose original STEP entity IDs for edges. The input-record index and model-space vertex coordinates locate the measured endpoint.

Two runs per commit used the same macOS arm64 machine, compiler options, debug dependencies and private STEP file. The order was old, new, new, old. User CPU time for the complete import fell from 15.29–15.62 s on `7fd89ffe9` to 7.42–7.45 s on `a65a65671`. Elapsed time was 18.79–20.55 s and 8.87–8.95 s, respectively. Other builds were running on the host.

The normal import stops at the gap check. A separate diagnostic ran level 2 directly on the original 345-face solid. The check alone took 0.404 s and reported 11 findings. This single sample does not establish a false-refusal rate.

### Regression tests

- The synthetic box with a 0.0007 mm edge has a source gap of 0.0008 mm. Healing increases it to 0.001063 mm. Recovery preserves all 13 edges and the box meshes at a 0.005 mm chord target.
- The ordinary healed box keeps 12 edges and has no source-recovery note.
- A box with an excessive source gap reports the measured gap, the limit, the independently identified edge and vertex, and the healed gap.
- A source that meets the endpoint limit but fails full geometry validation is refused.

### Verification and limits

- The quick gate against `origin/main` passed all 15 steps and 114 tests on `a65a65671`. All-target kernel Clippy passed with warnings denied.
- A successful level 2 recovery through the normal importer has been exercised on the synthetic box. The cost and acceptance rate of recovery on other production models are unmeasured. The GUI and MCP were not rerun on this build. The release-mode heavy gate is pending before this draft is marked ready.
- The fallback applies to STEP exchange. Solidcraft keeps its existing persisted-model import contract. A net loss of edges triggers the fallback. If healing removes an edge and adds another, the count can conceal the loss and the ordinary gap refusal still applies.

The issue stays open for the decision about viewing a model whose source exceeds machining tolerance.

Effort: high

Changelog: STEP import preserves validated short edges when healing would exceed the endpoint tolerance. An over-limit source refusal locates the worst endpoint and reports both measurements.

Refs #3252

title: fix(wire): allow sharp inside corners at the wire radius
body:
## What changed

- A Wire Contour has a new per-operation option: `sharp_corners`. The default is off.
- Off: the behaviour does not change. A sharp inside corner is refused by name, as before.
- On: the cover law accepts an uncut rest up to the kerf offset (wire radius + spark gap). A sharp inside corner of 60 degrees or more keeps no more than that.
- The worst accepted rest is a note on the path (`wire EDM: sharp inside corners stated - ...`).
- The post's wire verify line also says the note. It is not a refusal.
- A rest past the kerf offset is still refused. The message says that the option was on.
- The option is in these places:
  - the project file (`sharp_corners`, absent when off, so old files read unchanged);
  - the wire page, Geometry tab ("Sharp inside corners at the wire radius"), applied by `EditOperationParams`;
  - MCP `edit_operation`, through the params DTO (no new tool is necessary).
- The 4-axis cut does not read the option. It keeps its own `heal_tolerance`.

## Cause

The cover law in `motion::wire_edm::laws` had one rule: each profile point must be within the kerf offset of the wire path. A sharp inside corner always breaks that rule. The report's known-good Sodick program cuts a sharp 10 mm square, and the corner takes the wire radius.

## Tests

- `motion` lib `wire_edm::sharp_tests::a_sharp_square_die_is_cut_when_sharp_inside_corners_are_stated`: a sharp 10 mm square die with k = 0.162 mm. Off is refused with the issue's numbers (0.1620, 0.0671). On is cut, with the note and rest 0.0671. The wire corner stays k from both sides. A punch gets no note.
- `motion` lib `wire_edm::sharp_tests::an_inside_corner_past_the_wire_radius_stays_refused`: a 30-degree corner stays refused with the option on.
- `app` `wire_sharp_corners::a_sharp_square_die_is_cut_and_verified_with_its_corner_rest_as_a_note`: the command path, generation, the verify line, the project round trip, and undo.
- `ui` lib `wire_page_tests::wire_sharp_inside_corners_toggle_applies_and_undoes`: the checkbox, Apply and undo.
- Red before the fix: the pins did not compile (the option did not exist). On unchanged code, the sharp die is refused (the existing test `a_corner_tighter_than_the_wire_is_refused_by_name` pins that).
- Mutation checks (each red, then green after the restore):
  - `sharp_reach` gives 0 when the option is on (the old law): `a_sharp_square_die_is_cut_when_sharp_inside_corners_are_stated` is red.
  - `sharp_reach` has no bound (1e9): `an_inside_corner_past_the_wire_radius_stays_refused` is red.
  - The verify line does not add the note: `a_sharp_square_die_is_cut_and_verified_with_its_corner_rest_as_a_note` is red.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on head 543e9f1f8: 638 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.cl` or `.nc` file changed. The other test changes add `sharp_corners: false` to struct literals only.

## Not exercised

- The open run's own mitre-fold check (`open::offset`) does not change. An open run with a very short segment at a sharp corner can still be refused there.
- The 4-axis cut ignores the option.
- No run on a real control.

## Overlaps

- The open draft chain #2972, #2974, #2978, #2979, #2981, #2992, #2993 and #2999 adds other fields to the same `WireContourOp` literals in `crates/app/tests/*` and `wire_edm_dto.rs`. It touches the same files, but different fields. Whichever merges second refreshes. Each conflict is two added lines.
- #3205 and #3219 touch `wire_verify.rs`, in different functions.
- #3058 touches `open.rs`, in different functions.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3207-wire-sharp-corners.md`.

Changelog: Wire Contour can accept sharp inside corners at the wire radius (new per-operation option, default off); the corner leftover is said as a note in the path and the verify line.

Fixes #3207

### Station results

The public CLI produced the following files. A byte comparison matched each file to the original input for the HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 programming station, NC software `606425 004 SP20`.

| Sample | Blocks | Programmed stops reached | Test Run result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Single-tool XY arc contour | 41 | 3 of 3 | Program end |
| Two-tool contour with flood coolant | 63 | 5 of 5 | Program end |

Both files passed the controller converter's round trip with zero normalized block differences. Neither run logged an NC error. Configuring the station's release as a post target still gives a refusal. Qualification of a release requires separate evidence for the full supported scope.

### Checks on the target machine

The target manual describes the active travel limit for `M140 MB MAX` in §7.4, p. 303. Cycle 247 does not activate the preset in Test Run (§8.9, p. 492). On the physical Picomax, check the populated XYZ preset and coordinate state, tool and holder clearance, quill and drive state, tool table and coolant. The machine definition gives rapid rates. The installation's cutting-feed ceiling and machine-coordinate travel limits remain open. [HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 manual for 340 49x-03](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/iTNC530/34049x-neu/en/bhb.pdf)

title: fix(post): wire-iso writes each dimension word with a decimal point
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps` writes each dimension word with a decimal point. This applies to X, Y, U, V, I, J and the taper angle word. Examples: `X5.`, `Y0.`, `U0. V0.`, `FX-ANGLE A3.`.
- Trailing zeros are still removed (`X-20.165`). A negative zero writes `0.`.
- A new helper `pt()` does this. It uses the same rule as the Sodick wire post.
- The comment text keeps its plain numbers (`Z12` in the taper note).

## Cause

`fu()` used `trim()`, which removed the point from a whole number. Many wire controls read a number without a point in the least input unit (0.001 mm). On such a control `X5` moves 5 um, not 5 mm.

## Tests

- New pin: `wire_iso_decimal::every_wire_iso_dimension_word_carries_a_decimal_point`. It reads each wire-iso golden and refuses a bare X, Y, U, V, I, J or A word. Each golden is locked to the posted output by its own test.
- New check of the checker: `wire_iso_decimal::the_word_check_sees_a_bare_word_and_passes_a_pointed_one`.
- Red before the fix: yes. 21 bare words, for example `wire_slug_punch.nc:18: X-30 in G1 X-30 Y0`.
- Mutation 1: the old `wire-iso.cps` with the goldens written again. The pin is red. Restored: green.
- Mutation 2: only the angle word goes back to `trim()`. The pin is red on `FX-ANGLE A3`. Restored: green.
- Updated asserts that name the new words: `wire_post`, `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_4axis`.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 734 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. The post crate changes only a golden.

## Goldens moved

Nine goldens move. In each one only the decimal point changes. I checked this with a diff that removes the point and compares the lines: no line is left over.

`docs/decisions/3206-wire-iso-decimal-point.md`: the point is always on. A machine option to remove it was dropped.

title: fix(sim): judge a wire taper at the model's chord tolerance, refuse an undercut

## What changed

- A constant-taper Wire Contour is judged under the model's chord tolerance. The tolerance is the importer's chord promise (0.005 mm). A model that records a coarser chord uses that chord. 4-axis cuts keep their stated tolerance (#1170).
- The report line and a gouge name "the model's chord tolerance" for such a cut. Stated tolerances keep the old words.
- A new undercut law (`sim/src/verify/wire/undercut.rs`) judges the last pass of a constant-taper cut. A move that cuts a drafted wall at one judged height must cut it at every height. If it stands off the wall past the tolerance at another height, the post is blocked with `wire undercut: the kerf of move N stands ... mm off the part ...`.
- The law skips a move on a vertical wall. A taper on a vertical wall is a stated relief, as in the #536 and #1164 fixtures.
- `WireJob` has a new field `taper_chord`. `WireFinding::Gouge` has a new field `chord`. `WireVerdict` has a new field `chord`. The test literals get `taper_chord: false`.

The generator lays the tapered wire from the section at one height. The facets at the other heights stand off the true cone by up to their chord. title: feat(deburr): chord width, Constant Depth sizing and multi-pass breaks
body:
## What changed

- A 3D Deburr `width` is now the chamfer chord `w = 2 s sin(theta / 2)` across each edge. `theta` is the wedge angle of the edge. The setback `s` and the tip drop `s / tan(half-angle)` come from the wedge of each edge. `Chamfer2D.width` does not change.
- New `finishing3d::DeburrBreak` (in the new `deburr_size.rs`). `DeburrParams` and `OpParams::Deburr` each get one field, `sizing`, which holds:
  - `mode`: `ConstantWidth` (default) or `ConstantDepth` (`s = d / cos(theta / 2)`).
  - `depth`: the depth that Constant Depth holds on each edge.
  - `profile`: `Chamfer` (default) or `Round`.
  - `passes`: 1 to 100.
- Passes go from the outer pass to the final pass. Pass `k` of `n` cuts the setback `s * k / n`. Only the final break is declared as an `EdgeBreak`, and each pass stays above it.
- A Round profile refuses by name: "a Round break profile needs a ball-tipped cutter, and the chamfer mill is a sharp cone".
- Runs chain only edges that have the same drop. Thus each run keeps one depth and one declared break.
- Range limits: Constant Width sizes wedges from 30 degrees up. Constant Depth sizes wedges up to 150 degrees. The ride skips an edge outside the range, and a note gives the count.
- The project file goes from v74 to v75. A v74 Deburr `width` is multiplied by `sqrt(2)` at load. On a 90-degree edge the cut depth stays the same. The new keys are `break_mode`, `break_depth`, `break_profile` and `passes`. They are always written, and an absent key reads as one Constant Width chamfer pass. MCP gets the keys from `ParamsDto`.
- The record bound (`stock_sim_breaks::declared_width`) and the flute-length door now use the largest setback of the size law (`DeburrBreak::max_setback`).
- UI: the Deburr Geometry tab has new rows: Break mode, Break width or Break depth, Break profile, and Number of passes.
- The cache stamp digests the sizing only when it is not the default.

Note for the maintainer: the issue text says v61 to v62. Main was at v74, so this PR uses v74 to v75. The meaning of `width` changes for new operations and for MCP clients: the same number now cuts a smaller break (by `sqrt(2)` on a 90-degree edge). Project files are migrated. Decide if the title needs `!`. The decisions are in `docs/decisions/1890-deburr-chord-width.md`.

## Cause

Before this PR, `width` was the radius of the cone at the edge's level. That is the setback on a horizontal face, not the chamfer width on the edge. There was no depth mode and no multi-pass mode.

## Tests

New pins:

## Change

Use `camcraft-cli export-agie-inspection <project> <operation> <new-directory>` for a saved operation.

A user can create an unassigned wire inspection operation on the Post page and choose one placed, closed DXF chain and an internal start. The user can save the operation and export a native Classic Cut 2S ISO/SBR/SBL directory with zero working steps. The CLI and MCP use the same entry points.

The exporter preserves the nominal line and circular arc geometry. It checks the source selection, closure, winding, rounding, arc extrema, start disk and supported mounted machine axes. It refuses a changed or unsuitable selection and a destination that exists. An inspection work does not become a qualified machining operation.

This first setup uses 10 mm height, a 3 mm internal start and a 0.25 mm wire. The reference piece has unknown physical X/Y dimensions. Its controller fields store zero length and breadth. The receipt identifies the unverified fixture, erosion settings, physical Z and perpendicular controller lead. It describes the controller’s quality request separately from an assigned erosion process. The nominal setup does not promise a historical start seam, lead or cut sequence.

Commit `d982d452b` merges upstream main at `4e0c81964` into the contributor branch. The only manual resolution was the generated MCP reference. The compiled registry and the published reference list the same 119 tools. A trial merge with main at `6308a5db5` completed without conflicts.

Part 1 of 2 for #3098. This change records which control a machine has. The post in #3182 will use these facts to select a supported dialect.

- A machine can state its control model, exact NC software release, installed options and tool-change procedure. An omitted option list means the options are unknown.

- The Picomax 55 definition describes three-axis CNC operation with W fixed, NC software `340490-03` and manual tool changes. It leaves the absolute travel limits and installed software options unspecified.

### Evidence and outstanding checks

The target manual describes the retract in §7.4, p. 303 and the preset in §8.9, p. 492. The retract uses the active travel limit. Cycle 247 does not activate a preset in Test Run. [HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 manual for 340 49x-03](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/iTNC530/34049x-neu/en/bhb.pdf)

The earlier Klartext prototype produced two programs for this installation. On the programming station running `606425 004 SP20`, both reached the end. The converter accepted 41 and 63 blocks. The station reached all three and five programmed stops. The physical machine still needs checks for the preset, quill position, retract clearance, drive state and coolant. This PR adds the machine data. The second PR supplies the writer and its golden programs.

### Verification

The review fix advances the saved project format from 74 to 75. Fields absent from a v74 file stay unspecified. The writer now records v75 so that older builds refuse the project before any machine facts can be lost.

Two actual CLI builds exercised this change. A pre-PR v74 build opened a v75 Picomax project and exited 1 with `unsupported project version 75 (this build writes 74)`. The revised CLI loaded an actual v74 VMC project and saved it at v75. A comparison found that its entire machine record stayed identical. title: ci(post-merge): one independent run per merge
body:
This PR needs the maintainer's decision. It changes a workflow in `.github/`. The runner tokens for more `camcraft-post-merge` runners come separately; this PR adds no secret and no repository variable.

## What changed

- `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`: the concurrency group is per commit, `post-merge-${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}`, with `cancel-in-progress: false`. Each push runs on a free `camcraft-post-merge` runner and always finishes. The `gate` job does not change.
- The `report` job has its own concurrency group, `post-merge-report`, with `cancel-in-progress: false`. Its checkout uses `fetch-depth: 0`.
- `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` keeps the last reported commit in a hidden marker in the rolling issue body: `<!-- post-merge-last-sha: <sha> -->`.
  - The script reads the marker from the newest rolling issue, open or closed.
  - If this commit is an ancestor of the marker commit and is not the same commit, the script prints a notice and reports nothing (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`).
  - Otherwise it reports as before and writes the marker. A new red issue carries the marker in its body. A green run with no open issue writes the marker into the last closed issue.
  - If git cannot resolve a sha, the script reports as before.
- The red issue text now says that each run gates exactly one commit.
- `docs/decisions/3184-post-merge-per-commit.md` records the decision.

## Cause

One concurrency group for `main` let one run go at a time. A second push waited, and a third push cancelled the waiting run. A red run then covered several merges, and the breaking merge needed a bisect (#3111).

## Tests

Pins (all in xtask):
- `post_merge_concurrency::post_merge_runs_each_commit_on_its_own`: the group is per commit and `cancel-in-progress` is false.
- `post_merge_concurrency::post_merge_reports_one_at_a_time_with_full_history`: the report job has group `post-merge-report`, `cancel-in-progress: false` and `fetch-depth: 0`.
- `post_merge_report::order::*` (6 tests, unix only): the real script runs against a temporary git repository with two commits and a fake `gh` that records each call.
  - `an_older_green_run_never_closes_a_newer_red_issue`
  - `an_older_red_run_never_reopens_after_a_newer_green_run`
  - `a_newer_green_run_closes_the_issue_and_moves_the_marker`
  - `a_green_run_without_an_open_issue_records_its_commit`
  - `a_new_red_issue_carries_the_marker`
  - `the_same_commit_reports_again`

Mutation results:
- The upstream script with the new tests: 5 order tests red. The new script: 7 of 7 green.
- The upstream workflow: 2 of 2 concurrency tests red. The new workflow: 2 of 2 green.
- The guard without the "not the same commit" check: `the_same_commit_reports_again` red. Restored: green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (xtask unit tests). `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- No real Actions run. The workflow change runs only after a merge to `main`.
- The real `gh` with `--jq`. The fake `gh` returns the final values directly.
- GitHub keeps at most one pending job in a concurrency group. If three report jobs wait at once, GitHub cancels the middle one, and that report is lost until the next run on `main`. The decision file records this limit.
- The `runners` skill (`.claude/skills/runners/SKILL.md`) still says "A group of merges tests only the newest head". The edit of that file was refused in this session (a protected path). A follow-up must change that line.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes these files.

title: feat(tools,app): cutting data for wood, MDF, plywood, acrylic and HDPE
body:
## What changed

- The cutting table has six new work materials: `softwood`, `hardwood`, `mdf`, `plywood`, `acrylic` and `hdpe`.
- Each new row has a cutting-speed window and a 10 mm chip load for HSS and carbide. Each row also has Kienzle constants.
- The new rows are appended. The table is indexed in `WorkMaterial::ALL` order. A project file stores the word, so old files read the same.
- New module `crates/tools/src/cutting_router.rs` gives the router chip load by cutter diameter. The points are 3 mm 0.30, 6 mm 0.65, 10 mm 1.0 and 12 mm 1.15 of the 10 mm chip load. Below 3 mm the scale falls in proportion to the diameter. Above 12 mm it holds.
- `WorkMaterial::chip_scale(d)` selects the router curve for a router material. It selects the existing metal bands (`fz_scale`) for the other materials.
- `app::cutting::compute` uses `chip_scale`. On a router material, a V-bit (`ToolKind::Taper`) reads its chip load at half its diameter.
- The turning table has the same six rows, because it is also indexed in `ALL` order.
- The `camcraft-tools speeds` command, the MCP tool descriptions, the generated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the `camcraft-mcp` skill list the new words.

The rpm clamp is the existing code in `compute`. It clamps to `spindle_min` and `spindle_max`. It then calculates the feed again at the clamped rpm, so the chip load stays the same. It names each clamp in `notes`. This PR does not change that code. The new tests pin it for a router spindle.

## Cause

The table had only aluminium, steels, cast iron, brass and POM. A router user who cut wood or plastics got no suggestion, or a suggestion from a metal row. The metal bands also give each cutter from 3 to 6 mm the same chip load. For wood, that is approximately two times too much for a 1/8 in cutter.

## Tests

New suite `crates/app/tests/cutting_router.rs`:

- `router_materials_have_words_and_round_trip`
- `each_router_material_matches_the_hand_calculation_on_a_6mm_end_mill`: S and F for each material against a hand calculation.
- `end_mill_v_bit_and_ball_nose_stay_inside_a_router_spindle`: end mills of 3, 6 and 12 mm, a V-bit and a ball nose, for each material and tool material, on a 10000-24000 rpm spindle.
- `a_v_bit_reads_its_chip_load_at_half_its_diameter`
- `a_router_spindle_clamps_both_ways_and_keeps_the_chip_load`: 3 mm softwood is held at 24000 rpm, with F 4320. 12 mm HSS acrylic is raised to 10000 rpm, with F 2875. Each clamp is named.

Unit tests in `crates/tools/src/cutting_router.rs` pin the curve points, the ends and that the curve never falls.

Before the fix, the suite did not compile: the materials did not exist.

Mutations (each put back, each run, then restored):

- Old `crates/app/src/cutting.rs` (metal bands for all materials): 3 tests red.
- No half-diameter V-bit reading: `a_v_bit_reads_its_chip_load_at_half_its_diameter` red.
- `chip_scale` always returns `fz_scale`: 3 tests red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on the final head (24 steps). The first run had one expected red, `mcp_doc_drift`, because the MCP description changed. I generated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` again, and the suite is green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- material cutting` is green (7 tests), because the UI iterates `WorkMaterial::ALL`.

Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` ran on the final head `a022f26da77172be7524d3bf7dab8ac8de98ed84`. Result: 236 steps, 0 failed, wall 44.3 min.

- Step 1: the release build of `camcraft-motion` and `camcraft-app` (`--no-run`).
- `motion` heavy lanes: 37 steps, all green.
- `app` heavy lanes: 198 steps, all green.
- Known-fail markers stayed red as expected: #1950 (3 tests) and #2849 (2 tests).

## Goldens moved

None. The metal rows use the same expression as before, so their S and F do not change.

## Not exercised

- I did not start the GUI. The material lists in the UI come from `WorkMaterial::ALL`, and their unit tests are green.
- The turning rows for wood and plastics have only the table-order test. No lathe test uses them.
- The numbers are our own conservative values at the low side of public woodworking and plastics ranges. A human must still check them against a real router cut.

## Overlaps

- #3151 changes `crates/app/src/cutting.rs` in `feed_mut`. This PR changes `compute` in the same file. The functions are different. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/3068-router-materials.md`.

Process change: yes

Effort: high

Changelog: Cutting data for softwood, hardwood, MDF, plywood, acrylic and HDPE, with the chip load by cutter diameter and the router spindle clamp.

Fixes #3068

title: feat(ui): show the operator side at the work envelope
body:
## What changed

The viewport now shows the operator side of the work envelope. An arrow starts at the lower edge of the operator-side face. The arrow points out of the envelope, toward the operator. The text "Operator side" is at the tip of the arrow.

- `camcraft-post`: a machine file can state `general.operator_side`. The words are `"-X"`, `"+X"`, `"-Y"` and `"+Y"`. The word names the world axis that points from the envelope to the operator.
  - The field is optional. Old machine files and old projects load without a change.
  - A wrong word refuses the file by name. A wrong word never reads as the default.
  - `OperatorSide::default_for` gives the default of each machine kind: `+Y` for a lathe, `-Y` (the front) for each other kind.
- `camcraft-ui`: `operator_side.rs` builds the arrow when its input changes (the placed envelope and the side). Each other frame reads the kept arrow. The text is screen text, so it stays readable when the view turns.
- The View door has a new box, "Show operator side". It is view state: on by default, no command, not saved. It is disabled while the work envelope is off.
- The arrow and the text use the envelope colour. They are outside the envelope, so they do not cover the part or the toolpath.
- Docs: `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (the machine file grammar) and `docs/decisions/2632-operator-side.md` (the defaults for each kind).

title: feat(2d): V-Carve operation - depth from the region width along the medial axis
body:
## What changed

- A new 2D operation, **V-Carve** (kind tag 44). A V-bit carves a closed region. The tip follows the medial axis. At each point the depth is where the cone touches the two walls. A maximum depth (`Top Z - Bottom Z`) limits the cut.
- Motion kernel: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/vcarve.rs`, `vcarve_axis.rs`, `vcarve_walk.rs`.
  - The tip positions come from the largest inscribed circle at each sampled boundary point. The centre of that circle is a point of the medial axis.
  - The cone keeps a wall allowance of 0.01 mm. The kernel checks each straight feed move against the outline before it writes the move. A move that fails becomes a retract and a new plunge.
  - A branch into a corner that turns less than 20 degrees is not ridden. A tessellated circle is one dip, not a star.
  - Deep carves step down. An optional flat-clearing pass uses offset rings of the same V-bit inside the wall pass.
  - The cone height also limits the depth. The path carries a note when it does.
- App: the `VCarve` kind row, the generator arm, the seed, heights, the mark depth law (`DepthLaw::Mark`), the project-file arm `VCarve` (appended, no version step), posting and the setup sheet.
- Sim: a new `Mode::Carve`. It has the stand-downs of `Mode::Engrave`, and the crossing law is off. The walk rides each axis branch from its two walls, so the two rides lie on one another by design.
- UI: a V-Carve parameter page and an original icon (`assets/ui/op-v-carve.png`, `.svg`).
- MCP: the generic `add_operation` tool takes the kind `V-Carve`. `list_operation_types` lists the kind and its fields. No new MCP tool is necessary.
- The V-bit is the existing `Taper` tool kind. The included angle is the tool's `tip_angle`.
- Review correction: generation and stock simulation use `min(Top Z - Bottom Z, cone height)` for the V-Carve mark budget. Other marks keep their radius limit. A legal 60-degree V-bit cut can exceed the bit radius.

## Sources (literature)

The algorithm is written from these published sources. The module heads name them.

- H. Blum, "A transformation for extracting new descriptors of shape", 1967 (the medial axis transform).
- H. I. Choi, S. W. Choi, H. P. Moon, "Mathematical theory of medial axis transform", Pacific J. Math., 1997.
- J. Ma, S. W. Bae, S. Choi, "3D medial axis point approximation using nearest neighbors and the normal field", The Visual Computer, 2012 (the tangent-circle shrink).
- M. Foskey, M. C. Lin, D. Manocha, "Efficient computation of a simplified medial axis", 2003 (the separation angle).
- M. Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", 1991 (the floor rings).
- The cone law `depth = radius / tan(angle / 2)` is machine-tool handbook geometry.

The session had no web access, so no Perplexity search ran. camlib was a feature list only. No code or output of another program was read.

## Cause

There was no V-carve operation. The engrave ride follows a line at one depth only.

## Tests

- `crates/motion/tests/v_carve.rs` (11 tests):
  - `the_cone_never_leaves_the_region`: sweeps the cone along the path against the region outline.
  - `the_depth_follows_the_width_of_the_region`, `a_sharp_corner_rises_to_the_surface`, `a_stroke_is_cut_in_one_engagement`, `a_tessellated_circle_is_one_dip_not_a_star`, `the_maximum_depth_limits_the_cut`, `flat_clearing_removes_the_floor_the_cone_cannot_reach`, `a_deep_carve_steps_down`, `a_cone_shorter_than_the_maximum_depth_limits_the_cut_and_says_so`.
  - `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`: angle, diameter, maximum depth, stepdown, feed, clearance, retract, stepover, non-finite numbers, an empty region.
  - `degenerate_regions_give_a_clean_answer`: a fuzz set of 45 regions (zero width, a 1 micron sliver, a bow tie, a spike, far from the origin, 40 seeded random polygons), with and without flat clearing. Each gives a clean error or a path whose cone stays inside.
- `crates/app/tests/v_carve_op.rs` (8 tests):
  - `a_sixty_degree_carve_deeper_than_the_bit_radius_is_legal`: a 10 mm, 60-degree V-bit cuts 6 mm deep in a 20 mm square. Generation has no blocking warning. Stock simulation has zero gouge cells. The program posts.
  - `a_letter_is_carved_verified_simulated_and_posted`: the letter L generates, the program sim finds 0 gouge cells, and it posts.
  - `the_letter_matches_its_golden_cl_file`: golden `crates/app/tests/golden/v_carve_letter_l.cl`.
  - `the_operation_is_undone_and_done_again`, `a_tool_that_is_not_a_v_bit_is_refused_by_name`, `a_top_typed_under_the_surface_is_a_gouge_that_holds_the_post`, `a_saved_v_carve_opens_with_its_numbers`, `over_mcp_a_letter_is_carved_verified_and_undone`.
- Red before the change: yes. The pins do not compile on `main`, because the kind and `v_carve` do not exist there.

### Mutation checks

- New pin `a_sixty_degree_carve_deeper_than_the_bit_radius_is_legal`: restore the old radius budget at the generation call. The test fails with 20 `Gouge` warnings. Restore the cone budget: green.
- The same pin: restore the old radius budget at the `stock_sim` call. The test fails with 84 gouge cells. The worst gouge is 0.93676 mm. Restore the cone budget: green.

- `link_ok` in `vcarve_walk.rs` always returns true: `the_cone_never_leaves_the_region` is red. Restored: green.
- `VCarve` removed from the mark law (`mark_law.rs`): `a_letter_is_carved_verified_simulated_and_posted` and `over_mcp_a_letter_is_carved_verified_and_undone` are red. Restored: green.
- `Mode::Carve` with the crossing law on: the letter L is refused (checked in the earlier session, see the decision record).

- `operation::types::tilt_basis::tests::the_tilt_slot_covers_each_kind_whose_file_shape_has_a_tilt`: `tilt_slot` now covers `VCarve` (code change in `tilt_basis.rs`; main's #2599 added the slot after the held work).

## Gate

### Final-head validation

All results below apply to head `81aef5ab2935da80e6ebbe517216d4ccafe032bc`.

title: fix(2d): rest pass keeps corner reliefs on the rest center boundary

## What changed

- `rest_pocket_with_relief` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest2d.rs`) keeps a planned corner relief when its start is in the rest center area grown by 0.01 mm (`RELIEF_START_TOL`).

- The decision record is `docs/decisions/3146-rest-relief-boundary.md`.

## Cause

The old filter was `.filter(|r| plan.center.contains(r.start))`. Each relief start is a vertex of the pocket's own center area. title: fix(multiaxis): refuse a work-turning rotary line off the WCS origin
body:
Stacked on #3125 (merge #3125 first).

## What changed

- New function `posting::index_swing::off_origin`. It is true when a rotary states a `pivot` or an `offset` that is not zero, or not finite.
- The index-swing clause (`posting_index_swing::verdict`) has a new verdict `OffOrigin`. A work-turning rotary with a level line and an off-origin `pivot` or `offset` refuses the post by name. With two or more work-turning rotaries, any off-origin rotary refuses.
- The posed first-traverse law (`operation::first_traverse_posed::turn_of`) refuses generation by name in the same cases.
- One vertical work-turning rotary with a pivot is not refused. A turn about a vertical line keeps every height.
- A zero `pivot` or `offset` is judged as before.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3127-offset-rotary-line.md`.

## Cause

The two clauses read each work-turning rotary line through the WCS origin. A machine file can state a `pivot` or an `offset` that moves the line. The clauses then read the swept set about the wrong line. The reading can be too low, and the post is not blocked.

`pivot` is in machine coordinates. The project does not state where the WCS origin is in machine coordinates. So the program cannot place the moved line. A refusal is the safe answer.

- `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_posed.rs`:

title: fix(slot): cut the round ends of a slot wider than the tool
body:
## What changed

- A Slot wider than its tool now runs one wall lap at each level, after the rows.
- The lap follows the boundary of the tool centre stadium: two straight sides and two half circles.
- Each half circle is a chain of arcs (G02/G03). The chain is split at every row end on it and at its tip, so no arc is more than 90 degrees.
- The rows and the lap compute a row end with one function (`cap_point`). Each row join meets the lap at the same point to the bit.
- The lap starts where the last row ends and closes at that point.
- Under `climb` the lap is counterclockwise (the slot's air on the left, the same sense as the rows). Under conventional it is clockwise.
- A full-width slot (`h = 0`, one row on the centre line) does not change.
- The lap code is in the new module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_lap.rs`. `slots.rs` is 394 lines.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2906-slot-round-ends.md`.

## Cause

A row touches a round end only at its end point. The move between two rows is a straight line. The tool did not follow the arc between two row ends. On a 10 mm slot with a 6 mm tool, 0.86 mm stayed on the wall of each round end.

## Why the arcs are split at the row ends

The first version used two quarter arcs for each cap. The quick gate refused it on 8 app suites. The verifier's crossing law (a) flattens an arc into chords inside its circle. A row join is a chord that ends exactly on the circle, so it crossed those flattened chords, and the post was held. With the split, the join and the lap share their vertices. The law reads a shared vertex as a touch, not a crossing. The crossing law does not change.

## Tests

- New pin: `crates/motion/tests/slot_round_ends.rs`
  - `wide_slot_cuts_its_round_ends_climb`
  - `wide_slot_cuts_its_round_ends_conventional`
  - `wide_slot_with_rows_off_the_tips_cuts_its_round_ends`
  - Each point on the stadium wall must be within the tool radius of the tool centre path (limit 0.01 mm). No tool centre point may leave the cutter centre stadium. `crossed_pairs` (the verifier's crossing law) must be empty.

- New unit tests in `slot_lap.rs`: the lap closes on its start; each row end is a lap vertex; CCW from `b` runs the +n side first; CW from `b` turns round `b` first.
- Mutations repeated on head `35020f6cc294c3b6266be720b3c9d2b178c970f9`:

title: fix(kernel): measure a fan at a spline pole by its true sag
body:
## What changed

- New module `crates/kernel/src/mesh_pole.rs`. It finds a triangle corner that sits on a pole of a spline face. At a pole, the derivative along one parameter is zero.
- The module moves the free parameter of that corner to the mean of the other two corners. It takes those two corners on one side of the period.
- The module keeps the move only when the surface point stays within 1e-9 mm.
- `mesh_deviation::face` calls the module for spline faces before it samples a triangle. Analytic faces do not change.
- New fixture `testdata/models/sphere_quarter_pole.step`. This is our own file: a quarter sphere, R 25, with a rational B-spline dome that turns 180 degrees and ends in a pole at the apex.

## Cause

The issue reports an open mesh on v0.24.0. On upstream/main 8be100737 (after #917), the import itself refuses the q02 part:

```
solid #3738 'Mould' could not be tessellated: machining mesh: face Some(10) stands 5.089e-1 mm off its surface, tolerance 5e-3 mm
```

Face 10 is the ellipsoid boss (`#3666`, a rational B-spline with a pole at its top). The mesh is good. Its sag against the ellipsoid is about 0.004 mm. The planner gives the apex node u = 0 (and u = 1), and the ring under it has u near 0.5. The measure interpolated u across half the period in each fan triangle. It then projected from a hint on the far side of the surface. The bound of those triangles became 0.29 mm. The bound did not change at a finer chord. title: fix(2d): read a drafted side as a wall, not as a modelled chamfer
body:
## What changed

- A no-pick 2D chamfer now reads a drafted side as a wall. It does not read it as a modelled chamfer.
- The chamfer takes a third section of the material, half way between the top plane and the corner plane.
- A piece of a top loop is a drafted wall when two conditions are true:
  - It stands off the wall by no more than `depth * tan(15 deg)`.
  - The half-depth section stands half that distance off the wall within `LEAN_SLACK` (0.0001 mm). This check limits the departure from a straight wall.
- A loop with drafted pieces and no bevelled piece rides its wall at the corner depth. It counts with the sharp loops (#2596). Thus a plate with no modelled chamfer breaks every edge, the drafted side and the pocket included.
- `partly_bevelled` becomes `read`, which returns a `Reading`. The #2887 refusal text does not change.
- `ride_loops` takes two new arguments: `mid` (the half-depth section) and `depth`. The one caller, `material_source.rs`, makes the half-depth section.

## Cause

PR #2894 refuses a loop that is bevelled on only part of its length. It reads each piece more than 0.05 mm off the wall as "bevelled". A drafted side also stands off the wall. With a 1 mm chamfer and a 90 degree cone, a draft of more than about 3 degrees is more than 0.05 mm off. The plate was refused with a "modelled chamfer" message.

Two sections cannot tell a draft from a small modelled chamfer. A third section checks the straight slope within the section grid slack. A draft puts the half-depth section at half the offset. A modelled chamfer that ends before the corner plane departs from this slope. The review found that a 25% residual allowance admitted a 0.25 mm bevel that ends at 0.7 mm depth. The check now uses `LEAN_SLACK` (0.0001 mm).

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride_tests.rs`:

- `a_plate_with_one_drafted_side_rides_its_wall`: #2887's plate with its X0 side drafted 3.5, 5 and 10 degrees. Red on unchanged code: `the edge loop near X0.087 Y20.000 carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length`.

- `a_bevel_ending_below_half_depth_is_no_draft`: the review fixture has a 0.25 mm bevel that ends at 0.7 mm depth. The test requires the partial-bevel refusal for a 1 mm ride.
- `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer`: a 45 degree bevel deeper than the ride is still refused.
- The #2887 tests (`a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name`, `..._with_an_extra_vertex_too`) still pass. The old test calls go through a small `ride` helper.

- Half-depth check off: `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft` red.
- Slope limit off: `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer` red.
- Drafted match arm after the vertex-gap arm: the 3.5 degree case of the drafted pin red (it rode the top loop, inside the part).

Review verification on head `5e745b74430e4186f3bf293a23aa8b462a217fba`:

- Mutation check for `a_bevel_ending_below_half_depth_is_no_draft`: RED with the former `d * 0.25` allowance (0 passed, 1 failed; exit 101). Restoring `LEAN_SLACK` gives GREEN: all 17 `chamfer_ride` library tests pass.

title: fix(2d): turn a contour seam lead only when it crosses its own ring
body:
## What changed
- New module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/lead_seam.rs` with `seam_tangents`.
- `lead_fit.rs` calls `seam_tangents` from `both_fit` and `plan_leads`.
- At the seam of a closed ring, the function builds the full lead along the walk's end tangent.
- It checks that lead against the ring's own feed moves. It uses the verifier's crossing law (`arc_cross::moves_cross_prior`).
- Only a lead that crosses gets a new tangent: the old tangent mirrored across the other end's tangent.
- The mirrored lead is used only if it does not cross.
- A lead that does not cross keeps its tangent. Open walks keep their tangents.
- New test file `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_lead.rs`.
- Decision record `docs/decisions/3019-contour-lead-cross-only.md`.

## Cause
- On the issue's R6 plate, the seam falls on a fitted corner arc.
- The 8 mm linear lead-out along that arc's end tangent crossed the ring's long bottom edge next to the seam. The lead-in did the same on a conventional cut.
- Verify found one crossing on each level. Tabs are not the cause: the same crossing occurs with no tabs.
- The first fix (#3053) mirrored the tangent on each closed ring that bent at the seam. That also changed plain rectangles with no crossing (#3111). #3114 reverted it.
- This fix changes a lead only when that lead crosses its own ring.

title: fix(motion): Circular climbs to clearance between its rings
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs`: before each ring after the first, the tool climbs straight up to clearance at the end of the last ring. Then the ring's ladder enters from clearance, as the first ring does. This applies to the flat mode and to the vault.
- The unit tests of `circular.rs` move to `circular_tests.rs` with no change. This keeps `circular.rs` at 361 lines (it was 411 before this PR).
- Two goldens gain the one new climb move.
- New pins in `crates/motion/tests/circular_ring_links.rs` and `crates/app/tests/circular_ring_links.rs`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2898-circular-ring-links.md`.

## Cause

Each ring runs its own level ladder (ring-major order). The first descent of a ladder expects the tool at clearance. After the first ring, the tool stood on that ring's floor. The descent then made one diagonal rapid from the floor up to clearance over the next ring's start. That rapid crossed the core that the next ring had still to cut. Verification convicted it and held the post. A 5 mm hole with a Ø6 tool has only one ring, so the catalog case did not show the fault. The vault had the same diagonal rapid.

## Tests

Pins:

- `the_link_between_circular_rings_clears_the_stock` (motion): plunge, helix and ramp entry; planar and default links; flat and vault. No lateral rapid under the stock top. The verifier convicts no rapid.
- `the_issue_case_climbs_to_clearance_between_its_rings` (motion): the issue's four rings (R 7, 5, 3, 1). Each traverse onto R 5, 3 and 1 is at clearance.
- `a_spliced_diagonal_link_between_rings_is_still_convicted` (motion): the real path is clean. A diagonal link of the old shape, spliced in, gets `RapidInStock`. This is the "post stays blocked for a deliberately unsafe link" part of Done.
- `a_multi_ring_circular_links_its_rings_over_the_stock_and_posts` (app): the issue's job through generate, verify and post. No warning, and the program posts, for the plunge and the ramp entry.

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code the app pin reports `RapidInStock { at: 69 }` and `RapidInStock { at: 119 }`, the moves that the issue names. The motion pin reports rapids under the stock top at moves 69, 119 and 169.

Mutation: the fix with the climb disabled makes all three motion pins red (the flat case and the vault case at moves 20 and 40). The fix restored makes them green.

Gate:

body:
## What changed

- A flat Circular with a helix entry turns the start of each later ring. The new start is a vertex of the ring's own polygon. At that vertex, the predicted helix orbit keeps 0.01 mm from the orbits that the earlier rings flew.
- After each ring, the kernel reads the descents that the ring flew. It uses the crossing law itself (`verify::crossed_pairs`, 0.01 mm and 0.001 mm chords). If a descent crosses a descent of an earlier ring, the operation is refused by name: `helix entry: the descent at ... crosses the descent of an earlier ring ...`.
- The first ring and each ring without a conflict keep vertex 0. Plunge entry, ramp entry and the vault mode do not change.
- The new logic is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular_helix.rs`.
- The test module of `circular.rs` moved to `circular_tests.rs` (the `#[path]` pattern). `circular.rs` was 411 lines. It is now 374 lines.

All rings of a flat Circular run the same level ladder. Thus the helix of each ring shares each level's depth band with the helix of each other ring. title: Publish SHA256SUMS.txt with every release
body:
## What

The release workflow's `publish` job now writes a `SHA256SUMS.txt` covering every release asset and uploads it with the other files.

- A new step runs `sha256sum` in `dist/` over the same file patterns the job already publishes (zip, setup.exe, tar.gz, deb, rpm, dmg, AppImage, snap, flatpak, pkg.tar.zst), checks the result with `sha256sum -c`, and prints it to the log.
- `dist/SHA256SUMS.txt` is added to the `softprops/action-gh-release` file list.

The file uses standard `sha256sum` format (`<hash>  <filename>`), so users can verify a download with:

```
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS.txt
```

## Why

I've asked for CamCraft to be added to ArtCraft Launcher as a community app (storytold/craft-launcher#1545). The launcher checks every download, including downloads of community apps, against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so CamCraft can't be listed until its releases include one. Checksums also help anyone who downloads the files by hand.

Releases that are already published don't change. The file will appear starting with the next tag.

## Testing

- The YAML parses.
- I ran the step's script on sample files: it lists each asset once, `sha256sum -c` passes, and `release-body.md` isn't included.
- I haven't run it in a real release. That will happen on the next tag.

- After: `the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown position at the clearance height 30.000 mm, under the stock top at 31.114 mm (both measured along the tilted tool axis) - raise the clearance height by at least 1.114 mm`

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

- A new SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads an SVG file into the same `dxf::Document` as the DXF reader. The sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, the `Sketch` entity and the project file are shared and do not change.
  - Elements: `path` (M L H V C S Q T A Z, absolute and relative), `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `rect` (with rx/ry), `circle`, `ellipse`.
  - Groups: `g` with `transform` (matrix, translate, scale, rotate, skewX, skewY). A `use` of an element in the same file is drawn.
  - Curves: an arc or circle that maps to a circle stays an analytic arc. Beziers and true ellipses become lines within 0.005 mm.
  - Units: `width` and `height` in mm, cm, in, pt, pc or px (96 px to the inch), with the `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio`.
  - Y is flipped about the page height, so the drawing looks as it does in the editor.
  - A top-level `g` is a layer (`inkscape:label`, else `id`).
  - Text, images, nested `svg`, `style`, clip paths, masks, hidden content and `use` of other files are skipped and counted by kind.
- A new undoable command, `ImportSvg` (`commands/import_svg.rs`). It wraps `ImportDxf`, so apply and invert are the same code.
- A new MCP tool, `import_svg` (`mcp/svg_tools.rs`), and a new script verb, `cam.importSvg`. They take the options of `import_dxf`.
- The user guide (units and coordinates) and the MCP tool table list SVG.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals (by name, never a panic)

- A file that states no physical size, until the caller gives the unit of one drawing unit. The size is never guessed. A unitless `width` counts as no physical size.
- A caller unit for a file that states its size (two sizes would disagree).
- Malformed XML, malformed path data, an unknown transform or a singular one.
- A zero or negative document size or viewBox. A negative shape size.
- A degenerate arc (a zero radius).
- Percent or font-relative lengths in shapes.
- A file over the import budget (bytes, elements, segments), nesting deeper than 256, and `use` chains deeper than 16 (a reference loop).
- A compressed `.svgz` file, and a file that is not UTF-8.

## Tests

- `crates/geometry/tests/svg.rs` (9 tests): a rectangle with a hole in mm (nesting, Y flip), in and pt and px and cm documents, no physical size, absolute and relative path forms, Beziers and arcs, nested group transforms and a sheared ellipse, a rounded rect with polyline and skipped content, merged short segments, compact path syntax.
- `crates/geometry/tests/svg_refusals.rs` (5 tests): malformed documents and paths, zero or negative sizes, the import budget, and a deterministic smoke fuzz (truncations and 1000 byte mutations).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_svg.rs` (2 tests): `import_svg` end to end (units, layers, chains, skipped notes, bounds, move, undo and redo, a 2D Contour on the profile, save and reopen, the script verb), and the command's refusals and undo step.
- Red before the fix: the pins did not compile on unchanged code (`unresolved import camcraft_geometry::svg`).
- Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the pin went red, and then the guard was restored:
  - Y flip: red (4 tests).
  - Arcs stay analytic: red (4 tests).
  - Caller unit on a sized file is refused: red.
  - A unitless size is no physical size: red.
  - Zero-radius arc refusal: red.
  - `use` depth guard: red (stack overflow).
  - Short-segment merge: red.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean (exit 0).
- Touched suites, all green:
  - geometry: `svg` 9, `svg_refusals` 5, `dxf`, `dxf_refusals`, `sketch_data`, `sketch_chains`, and the lib tests.
  - app: `mcp_svg` 2, `mcp_dxf` 2, `sketch_profile` 8, `sketch_project` 14, `scripting` 20 (it checks `cam.d.ts`), `mcp` 23, and the lib tests (290).
- The gate did not complete. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` falls back to the batch tier, because the diff touches `crates/geometry/src/lib.rs`. On this machine the shared sccache server stopped responding: each compile through it hung, including the jobs of other sessions. The gate sets the sccache wrapper itself, so it hung at the `post` build twice. Clippy and the suites above ran with the wrapper unset. The batch tier still needs a run: the post-merge gate, or a reviewer's `pr-test.yml` run.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A posted G-code golden for a 2D Contour on an SVG profile. On `main`, a 2D Contour on a profile is accepted but does not generate yet: that is #1864 (PR #2716). Follow-up: #3042.
- The row for `import_svg` in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The edit was blocked as a sensitive file in this session. A maintainer session can add it. Then that PR needs `Process change: yes`.
- No UI change: the app has no DXF profile import dialog yet, so there is no file dialog to extend.
- Nested `<svg>` viewports, CSS stylesheets, text to outlines and embedded images are out of scope (the issue says so). They are counted as skipped.

## Overlaps

- #2773 (draft, needs-rework) changes the stock check in `ImportDxf::build`. This PR does not change `build`. `ImportSvg` has its own copy of that 10-line check, so it does not get the #2773 change. If #2773 merges first, `ImportSvg` must get the same change.

This PR adds the UI for DXF profiles over the #1862 commands (`ImportDxf`, `MoveSketch`, `DeleteEntity`). It follows the maintainer's scope change on the issue: the DXF door is on the Stock page, not on `Model > Open`.

- The Stock page has a new group "DXF profiles". It has the control "Add DXF profile…" (a `.dxf` file picker). The control is disabled when the active setup has no stock.
- The group lists each profile of the active setup with these controls:

  - "Hide profile" / "Show profile". This is view state, the same list as the browser eye.
  - "Delete profile". This queues one `DeleteEntity`.
- A `.dxf` file dropped on the viewport goes through the same import path. With no stock, the drop is refused by name: "drop refused: <file> is a DXF profile - make a stock first ...".
- A drawing without `$INSUNITS` opens the modal "DXF units". The modal shows the drawing size read in millimeters and read in inches, each with the size in the other unit. "Millimeters" or "Inches" runs `ImportDxf` with that unit. "Cancel", Escape or a backdrop click places nothing. The unit is never guessed.
- The status line shows the import summary: the name, the setup, the unit and its source (file or chosen), the layer count, the closed and open chain counts, the chains not chained, and the skipped entities by type.
- The browser shows each profile as a child row of its setup's Stock row (`Leaf::Sketch`), with the suffix "DXF profile" and the eye. A click opens the Stock page and selects the profile, so Del deletes it through the history.
- The viewport draws the profile lines, arcs and circles of the active setup on the stock top, at `sketch::world_pose`. Each free end of an open chain gets a magenta X. No curve uses that colour, so an open gap does not look closed.
- The overlay lines are cached by the sketch data `Arc` and the pose (`SketchLineCache` on `FrameCache`). A still frame builds nothing (crates/ui/AGENTS.md, frame cost).
- The operation page Source list offers the profiles of the operation's setup for a kind that `sketch_model::admits` (2D milling, plasma, wire EDM). A setup with a stock, a profile and no model can so have an operation on the profile.

title: feat(mcp): compact read modes and chat context budgets
body:
## What changed

MCP read modes for small context windows (`crates/app/src/mcp/`):

- `get_job` takes `summary: true`. The summary removes `machine.definition`. Each operation keeps only the `params` fields that differ from the kind defaults. Null and empty fields outside `params` are removed.
- `list_operation_types` takes `kind` (key or label) and `section`. An unknown name is refused with the valid names.
- `list_features` takes `compact: true`. Compact rows keep the id, the name and the pick facts. Counts replace the loops. The compact default `limit` is 25. The full default stays 500.
- `provider::tools_in(provider, ToolSet::Core)` gives a core set of 25 workflow tools. `tools(provider)` is unchanged.
- The new code is in `mcp/compact.rs`. `job.rs`, `features.rs`, `pick.rs` and `tools.rs` get small hooks only.

Chat worker limits (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/budget.rs`):

- A tool reply to the model is cut at 12000 JSON characters, with a hint that names the compact modes. The tool card keeps the full text.
- A request carries at most one viewport image (the newest).
- A turn stops after 12 model rounds. The old `MAX_TURN_STEPS` moved to `budget::MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` and now has a test.
- A request carries at most 6 earlier turns. When older turns are dropped, the latest `get_job` reply goes in front of the first kept prompt.
- A local endpoint gets the core tool set. A cloud endpoint gets the full table.

title: fix(post): leave Agie jobs unarmed until the loaded work quality is verified
body:
Stacked on #2993. Review the [quality-binding correction above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/feb802a77a99878951d5faf5ba2f41f65270c018...814dca499f9f9793f3c9e6bcd3eafab5f32e2022).

## Author gate status

The guarded source at cfc281268 passed the complete reached heavy gate, 247/247 steps in 58.1 minutes on macOS arm64. It includes the separate default-machine correction merged upstream in #3092. The mixed-condition regression passed in the 19-test Agie writer module. Both input orders received the exact error and no files.

On the corrected production source 766fc7109, the regular CLI exported all 20 synthetic jobs. Their 32 works and 72 native files matched the previous guarded outputs byte for byte. All 20 controller-review receipts matched. All 20 repeat attempts refused to replace an existing job and preserved every byte. This corpus is a software comparison. The real control checks below cover the stated representative jobs.

The full quick gate on 766fc7109 found the missing dedicated test suite for the built-in Agie CPS dispatcher. The next commit added the suite and its 11 expected refusal records. Passing each record requires the direct single-file post to fail with the native-job diagnostic and leave no NC file.

The final head is 814dca499. It changes only tests above cfc281268. On a real plasma stream and 1300PL machine, the Agie single-file dispatcher must fail with its specific native-directory diagnostic. The workspace must exclude the post from the plasma registry. The single-file smoothing test now uses the workspace's native-post predicate. With smoothing enabled, a mounted Agie punch must refuse the setup and create no job directory. The other posts retain their previous checks.

All 49 targeted tests passed on the final head: seven plasma, seven smoothing, 12 native app, 11 native dispatcher and 12 recorded-stream tests.

The original full quick on cfc281268 ran 1,013 steps in 80.6 minutes. All but the two cross-post tests passed, including strict Clippy. On 814dca499 the official failed-step replay selected both suites and passed both in 0.8 minutes. Each suite ran seven tests. The complete 247-step heavy result belongs to cfc281268. The whole quick and heavy gates have not been repeated on 814dca499.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 211105042b817a5b32fdf2c971d42e6d968297c6 --failed gate-logs/quick-20261121-023002
```

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test plasma_post_refusals --test smoothing --test agie_native
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
```

## Integration order

The maintainer requests a separate P1 change from main and a safety-tier review of each feature PR. The standalone zero-step encoder is #3104. The first workspace writer in #2951 uses it. Keep earlier feature drafts that still generate erosion steps on hold until each takes its own safety correction and review. The standalone machine template in #2948 has no writer.

## Gate commands and pinning tests

The earlier macOS bore fixture and missing operation name were reproduced on ba5ff0ae1 with these commands:

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 1d81b609c --only 'app suites: default_machine_missing'
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 1d81b609c --only 'app heavy: pocket3d_hsm'
```

The scoped CLI and native writer checks include:

- `native_punch_links_its_three_files_and_uses_the_uncompensated_contour`
- `every_punch_has_its_own_geometry_and_uses_the_requested_piece_quality`
- `nine_model_owners_resolve_all_resources_and_the_same_registered_quality`
- `qualified_qn2_heights_set_both_piece_and_work_with_stock_top_at_zero`
- `the_saved_condition_selects_the_exact_requested_quality`

A stale native quality can change the effective Ra, pass count and wire offsets while the controller formal check passes. A 40 mm Cobra trial bound the same 0.30 request to different existing records. The wrong selection ran three passes at 0.245, 0.165 and 0.140 mm. The intended selection ran four at 0.250, 0.170, 0.145 and 0.135 mm. A deliberately conflicting semantic name also defeated the returned handle and success-status checks after a new piece import.

CAMCraft now writes a complete native setup bundle and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. Geometry, start holes, work definitions and separation settings are present. The bundle records a stable quality name for the requested tuple and checks each assignment. The operator must review each effective native work in place before generating any machining steps. The operator can correct a mismatched quality without importing the piece again.

Check the actual wire, stock height, Ra, Tkm, Te and visible options in Work Details. For a mismatch, use Quality (Kwaliteit) and Define (Definiëren) on that same work. Confirm the requested values. Open Technology (Technologie), select TECCUT, and use Assign (Toewijzen) on the matching row. Check the individual working steps and their offsets before running GRAFICHECK and FORMALCHECK. The user guide gives the full procedure and the expected values for each supported setting. The native dialog exposes two of the three authored checkbox values.

On the deliberately polluted installation, a new import showed both works at [0]. FORMALCHECK reported a blocking technology error for each. Correcting Ra on the first work kept both at [0]. Explicit TECCUT assignment armed only the checked work. The installation retained the other unarmed work until its own review. The saved two-work piece then passed FORMALCHECK. GRAFICHECK produced 16 correctly ordered profile and separation blocks. All nine nominal faces had the verified 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm offsets. Both rough bridges measured 1.000 mm. The two cutting envelopes remained disjoint. The effective Ra 0.30 Berco process was checked independently at 15, 20, 40 and 80 mm. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 96 app tests, 18 native post tests and three geometry tests. The app count includes machine, machine library and posting suites. It exported 20 jobs with 32 works. All 52 geometry and resource files matched previous output. Each of the 20 piece files changed from automatic machining to setup-only. Each repeat export preserved every file. Strict Clippy passed for the app, post, UI and geometry libraries. The final source revision reproduced all 72 files and reported working_steps_generated=false for all 20 jobs. Later changes clarify the repeat-import result and pin the refusal for mixed wire conditions.

After manual release and plotting of both a mixed-radius Ra 0.30 piece and a rectangular Ra 0.35 piece, the tester reimported each exact SBL on its existing control. Each import created a new default-named piece with the intended ISO resource and zero steps. FORMALCHECK again reported technology undefined. The earlier named piece stayed separate. Select the newly created row and confirm its geometry and [0] before assigning the technology.

The real GUI status before the change reported the posted job. After the change it reports zero working steps, the requested targets, wire and stock values, and the required offsets. Both screenshots show the same synthetic cutoff job, DEMO2999, after the desktop Post command. The new receipt lists the control checks and the offsets of 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.

**Before · `feb802a77`**

![Earlier Post receipt reporting three files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/579ee692c2b26e6aca37776f5319067443c742a1/pr-2999/receipt-before.png)

**After · `814dca499`**

![Current Post receipt reporting zero working steps and the required control checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/579ee692c2b26e6aca37776f5319067443c742a1/pr-2999/receipt-after.png)

Changelog: Agie native jobs import with zero machining steps. Review each work's effective native quality and offsets before assigning its technology in Agie Control.

Fixes #2984

title: feat(wire): post a native Agie Classic Cut 2S job
body:
**This first writer now uses the zero-step encoder from #3104. The machine template and standalone encoder have merged. The contributor has addressed the desktop review comments. A maintainer re-check is pending.** Later feature drafts still need their own safety review before they can introduce machining behavior. A stale controller quality can change the effective finish, pass count and offsets.

This change builds on the machine template in #2948 and the standalone encoder in #3104. These branches are in a fork, so this PR targets upstream main. Review [the first-writer safety adoption above its integration parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/1ea87ebac0204f3613c3d2549692b4108f620f66...025ed4760e592c3401859a66285457021a98341b).

## Change

The desktop Post command and cam.post write a native Agie job directory with linked ISO, SBR and SBL files. CamCraft writes the nominal contour in Rust. The setup requests a resident quality and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. The post validates the work before it creates the destination. It publishes all three files together and preserves an existing directory.

The supported case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock. Select the Classic 2S template from #2948. Enter the AGIE_QN2 condition for Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire and cold die steel. Select the 1.0 mm separation cut explicitly. The template starts without an installed condition. A cut needs 0.4 mm clearance at each stock face and 3 mm of straight face on each side of the entry. Other contours, tapers, skims, custom X/Y travel limits and additional workpieces are refused.

## Reference material for review

The contributor's team wrote [Agie-CAM at 11b1bb9](https://github.com/qsmits/Agie-CAM/tree/11b1bb9ef2c752b94b6fefc1f0814acd2e030c42) and released it under the MIT license. This draft retains the license and copyright notice. The implementation reference documents observed controller examples for parts of the JEScript sequence and the resident technology selection. The published guides linked on #2945 give the file roles and some interface arguments. They do not document the full sequence and all defaults. Please review that source against the project rules before merge.

The controller supplies its own runtime and technology table. This PR includes the writer and original synthetic examples and expected output. It includes no controller image, vendor post, runtime library or technology database.

## Control verification

On the corrected writer, the normal CLI produced the same three CCSEP20 files as the independently verified import in #3104. Only the output stem was changed from the PUNCH40 example. The copy of the actual control showed the closed punch at zero steps. FORMALCHECK blocked it until the operator assigns technology. See [the file hashes and native work details](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3104#issuecomment-7055077111). The native bytes were tested once in that replay. No physical cut was made.

On successive imports, select the newly created piece. Match its ISO, start hole and zero steps to the intended setup. Verify the effective wire, height, quality and offsets before assigning TECCUT. Run the control's graphic and formal checks on the resulting steps.

On the earlier writer, the control plotted a rough pass and three trims after automatic generation. The measured offsets were 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. That historical result does not qualify an automatic release on this or another installation.

The synthetic example runs from the repository root:
```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/punch.camscript
```
Use a new PUNCH40 destination.

## Review changes on `f92e67857`

Commit `25e783b50` merged upstream main at `6fafa4e1f` into the contributor branch. GitHub reports the corrected head as mergeable. A local trial merge with upstream `60cb97a0b` also completed without conflicts.

On `45d6166e1`, 67 focused tests passed. Three desktop tests use the Post button and the synthetic punch. The success case checks the requested finish, all three output files and the zero-step control review. Each refusal case checks that the output directory stays empty.

- `native_post_dialog_writes_three_files_and_reports_the_required_work_checks`
- `native_post_dialog_refuses_an_invalid_job_name_without_writing_files`
- `native_post_dialog_refuses_per_operation_output_without_writing_files`

On that revision the quick gate passed 1,032 of 1,033 steps, including clippy. All 253 reached heavy steps passed. The only failed step was `post suites: comment_escape`. Its registry test expected a single text file from every post.

The final commit changes only `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs`. The test checks header escaping for all 19 text posts and checks the native directory refusal for Agie. On `f92e67857`, all 27 focused tests passed. The official quick replay selected the one failed step and passed it. The screenshot source, UI tests and production code are identical on these two revisions.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 6fafa4e1f
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 6fafa4e1f
# On f92e67857, use the quick log directory from the first command.
cargo xtask gate quick --base 6fafa4e1f --failed <original-quick-log-directory>
```

## Checks on reviewed revision `025ed4760` and its predecessors

At a08c802b6, all five writer tests, four standalone encoder tests and ten application integration tests passed. The normal PUNCH40 script reproduced the previous guarded ISO, SBR and SBL. A repeat export refused to replace them. Both PUNCH40 and the CCSEP20 variant returned `working_steps_generated=false` and the controller review.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib agie::tests::
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test agie_native
```

Pinning tests include `script_post_reports_the_required_control_review_and_zero_working_steps`, `stock_origin_and_fractional_setup_coordinates_are_refused_before_publication`, `the_native_files_match_the_control_checked_rectangular_punch` and `qn2_requires_the_rough_wire_size_in_the_mounted_condition`.

The earlier guarded head was 5bdbb5fe4. It includes the upstream diagnostic fix from #3092 and a dedicated recorded-stream suite for the Agie dispatcher. The single-file post entry point must refuse the Agie dispatcher. Each of 11 input streams checks the diagnostic, the failure exit code and the absence of NC output. The suite inventory also requires this post to have its own tests.

On 5bdbb5fe4 the recorded suite passed 12/12 tests. The dispatcher suite passed 11/11. All nine default-machine regression tests and all 19 native tests passed. The normal CLI and an independent Rust caller reproduced the checked setup files and the matching ISO. Both duplicate exports preserved all files. Against upstream 211105042, the full plan selects 1,017 quick steps and 251 reached heavy steps. These two full gates did not run on that head.

```sh

The final head 025ed4760 adds cross-post tests. The plasma suite now runs the direct Agie dispatcher and requires its native-directory refusal. The single-file smoothing test uses the same native-post predicate as the workspace. A mounted, otherwise valid Agie punch with smoothing enabled must report the setup-option error and create no directory. All 48 targeted checks passed on 025ed4760: seven plasma tests, seven smoothing tests, 11 native app tests, 11 dispatcher tests and 12 common recorded-stream tests. The two current images show the synthetic DEMO20 punch on review revision `45d6166e1`. The picker identifies the requested finish. After posting, the receipt reports zero working steps and lists the checks and technology assignment required on the control.

title: feat(2d)!: Slot and Trochoidal Slot read DXF sketch chains
body: Stacked on #2716 (merge #2716 first) This branch starts at the head of #2716 (`2e77ca0ee`). The diff against `main` shows the changes of #2716 too, until #2716 merges. The changes of this PR are the one commit `feat(2d): Slot and Trochoidal Slot read DXF sketch chains`. ## What changed - A `Slot` and a `Trochoidal Slot` now take one picked chain of a DXF profile (`FeatureSel::SketchChain` or a `SketchLayer` that holds one chain). - One closed line-arc slot outline seeds `a`, `b` and `width`. - One open straight chain is the centerline. It seeds `a` and `b`. The typed `width` stays. - The pick seeds in its own command (`CreateOperation`, `SetOperationGeometry`). One undo takes back the pick and the seed. This is the law of #1504. - Generation judges the stored slot against the picked chain. A slot that left its outline is refused by name. A slot whose ends are not the ends of its centerline is refused by name. - The verification and the stock simulation use the setup stock (`part_solid = false`), as #2716 does for the 2D Contour. - Slot parameters keep their two-point form. This branch writes project v74 for sketch selections and per-chain overrides. A v73 file steps up and keeps its protection. Older readers refuse v74 files. These picks are refused by name: - a closed chain that is not a slot outline (a rectangle, a circle): "is not a slot outline"; - an open chain that is not straight: "the picked centerline is not straight"; - more than one chain: "a slot on a DXF profile cuts one chain, and this selection has 2 chains"; - the whole profile as the source: "needs one picked chain"; - a channel narrower than the tool. The `Slot` refusal now gives the slot width and the tool diameter. Files: - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_line.rs` (new): `SlotBound::from_centerline`, `SlotBound::centerline` and the ends law. - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room.rs`: the `Room::Line` kind in each match of the room law. - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slots.rs`: the numbers in the "slot is narrower than the tool" refusal. - `crates/app/src/operation/slot_sketch.rs` (new): resolves the picked chain to a slot room, and holds the outline test. - `crates/app/src/operation/slot_pick.rs`: `slot_bound_of` reads sketch picks; `slot_from_picks` and `confine_slot` include the `Trochoidal Slot` on sketch picks; `slot_fit_of` describes a centerline. - `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs`: the job reads the slot room for a `Trochoidal Slot` on sketch picks, and its region is the authored stadium. - `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: the `Trochoidal Slot` arm judges the slot against the slot room. - `crates/app/src/operation/material_region.rs`: the preview does not read sketch slot picks as a region. - `crates/app/src/operation/contour_sketch_pick.rs`: `visit_src_chains` and `transform_chain_pts` are `pub(super)`. - `crates/app/src/sketch_model.rs`: the profile law admits picked chains for the two slot kinds. - `docs/decisions/1868-slot-dxf-sketches.md`: the decision. ## Cause `sketch_model::source_problem` refused picked chains of a profile for each kind but the 2D Contour. `slot_bound_of` refused sketch picks. The slot room had no centerline kind. ## Tests Pins, in `crates/app/tests/slot_dxf_sketch.rs`: - `a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size` - `a_trochoidal_slot_reads_the_same_outline` - `an_open_straight_chain_is_the_centerline_at_the_typed_width` - `picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name` Pins, in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_pins.rs`: - `a_centerline_room_holds_its_two_ends_and_refuses_other_ends` - `a_bent_short_or_doubled_centerline_is_refused_by_name` The four app pins were red on the unchanged code. Each failed with "picked chains of a profile are not supported yet". Readings from the outline pin (4 mm tool, 10 mm outline, centres (45, 25) and (75, 25)): - seeded ends (45.000, 25.000) and (75.000, 25.000), width 10.000 mm; - cutter centre X 42.000 to 78.000 and Y 22.000 to 28.000; - stock simulation: 0 gouge cells. Mutation results. Each mutation removes one guard. Each made a pin red. The restored code is green. | Mutation | Result | |---|---| | M1 outline area test off | red (`picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`) | | M2 one-chain rule off | red (same pin) | | M3 centerline straightness test off | red (same pin) | | M4 centerline ends law off | red (`an_open_straight_chain_is_the_centerline_at_the_typed_width`) | | M5 slot room judge off in the `Trochoidal Slot` arm | red (`a_trochoidal_slot_reads_the_same_outline`) | | M6 whole-profile refusal off | red (`picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`) | | M7 old profile law back | red (all four app pins) | | M8 old "narrower than the tool" text back | red (`picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`) | | M9 doubled-back centerline test off | red (`a_bent_short_or_doubled_centerline_is_refused_by_name`) | | M10 sketch read off in `slot_bound_of` | red (all four app pins) | Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-2716` on head `bd24b9328`, where `base-2716` is the head of #2716 (`2e77ca0ee`).
